question: Where were you born?
answer: Plainfield, in New Jersey, in 1837.

question: In what country lies your home?
answer: In the air, over all the earth.

question: What is your father's name?
answer: He was called Thomas Adams, and was born at Northallerton, in Yorkshire, in the year 1696. He was bred a weaver, and followed that trade in London, till disabled by the gout; after which he took to printing, and died in 1748, aged 51.

question: What was your father's station in life?
answer: , He was a tanner, sir, a master tanner.

question: What is your mother's name?
answer: She bears the name of Anna.

question: What tongue did you first speak?
answer: Answer-To that which the first man conversed with.

question: What other tongues can you speak?
answer: I can speak English, French, German, and Italian.

question: In what city do you dwell?
answer: It dwells in the same place that is called Hell.

question: What is your rank or station?
answer: Youare the first created spirit.

question: Who serves under you?
answer: Answers will be welcomed to this.

question: What is your calling in life?
answer: AnswerI am he whom the vulgar call the Prince of Darkness; I have the superintendence of all unconverted sinners, and I bring them with me to everlasting burnings.

question: Are you married, and to whom?
answer: I married a lady who brought me a fortune, the better to indulge in vicious courses.

question: What brothers have you, and what are their names?
answer: by name, and to the left hand.

question: Name the lands you have visited.
answer: We have visited France, Italy, Switzerland, Germany, and Holland.

question: What is the greatest city you have seen?
answer: YetI sawLondon in 1824, and I thoughtParis a far finer sight. I never was inPetersburg, or Vienna.

question: What seas have you sailed upon?
answer: have visited many parts of Europe, and parts of Africa and America. During a residence of three years in the latter country, I travelled from Marischal to Natchez, and from Philadelphia to Quebec.

question: What rivers flow near your home?
answer: The Rhone, the Arve, and the Arveiron, run through Sixt, a village not far from Macon, in Burgundy.

question: What mountains have you crossed?
answer: I have passed over the Alps, and visited Italy.

question: Is your native country hot or cold?
answer: Hot, as it lies in the torrid zone. The inhabitants are swarthy, and subject to great heats in the day, and intense colds in the night.

question: What people are your neighbours?
answer: The inhabitants of London, Manchester, Sheffield, Liverpool, Norwich, Canterbury, Plymouth, Exeter, York, Edinburgh, Glasgow, and Dublin.

question: Who rules the land where you were born?
answer: An absolute tyrant, to whom the people are slaves.

question: In what age do you live?
answer: In the nineteenth century.

question: Who is the greatest man of your age?
answer: To be a great man, I must have a good disposition, for, as I am, I could never become so. This reason is sufficient to keep me from being the greatest man, although the greatest men have generally been of as good dispositions as myself; a thing which, as far as I can observe, is very much owing to chance.

question: What God or gods do you worship?
answer: Answer to God, or gods, as the case may be.

question: Who taught you your trade?
answer: We do not care to learn, says the father of evil.

question: What was the first employment you ever held?
answer: It was to be one of the rebels that warred against heaven; and as there was at that time war in heaven, I did my best to promote it. I remember I was the forwardest of all the rebellious crew in assaulting the Divine Essence, and committing high treason against the Majesty of the Omnipotent.

question: In what dress do the people of your country go?
answer: The people of my country go for the most part in black; but upon Sundays and holy-days they put on clothes of a brighter and gayer colour.

question: What is the chief food of your country?
answer: The chief food of our country is beef and mutton.

question: What beasts are found in your country?
answer: Lions, tigers, hyenas, &c.

question: What great works stand in your country?
answer: Milton's Paradise Lost, Shakespeare's plays, Newton's Principia, the steam-engine, and the Wealth of Nations.

question: By what road did you last come home?
answer: By the way of Finchley.

question: Where does your family come from?
answer: From the land of darkness and death.

question: What name does your family bear?
answer: The family name is Milton.

question: What festivals do your people keep?
answer: They keep the great festivals of Easter and Whitsuntide, the former in commemoration of Christ's resurrection from the dead, and the latter of the descent of the Holy Ghost on the apostles. They also observe the feasts of the Annunciation of the blessed Virgin, of St Michael the Archangel, and of All Saints; and they have a great annual commemoration of all their deceased friends on the anniversary of their death.

question: What is the farthest place from home you have stood?
answer: Yes, my evil genius was at length prevailed upon to set me down in Italy.

question: In whose court or company have you been received?
answer: In the company of those, who, in their secret thoughts, either deride or disobey the laws of God.

question: What offices or honours have you held?
answer: I have been an officer in every Court in Europe, and have taken my share of honours and emoluments in each; in Russia, Prussia, Austria, Spain, and England. I have been prime minister, field marshal, and chamberlain; have been decorated with all orders, from that of St.

question: What famous men have you met?
answer: The men I met were: Napoleon, Talma, Chateaubriand, and Sir Humphry Davy.

question: Where were you when you first left your father's house?
answer: Poino, on Sunday, the 11th instant.

question: What city did you first see after leaving home?
answer: I first saw Alexandria.

question: What is the climate of the place you now live?
answer: The climate is most agreeable; temperate, healthy, and pleasant. I would not change it for any other upon the face of the earth.

question: What coin passes in your country?
answer: No coin is current except gold and silver.

question: What is written over the door of your house?
answer: theI will put a hook in thy nose, and a bridle in thy lips, and I will turn thee back by the way by which thou camest.

question: Who were your playfellows as a child?
answer: The playfellows of my childhood were of my own sex and age. Amongst the rest, two schoolfellows, whom I tenderly loved, and still revere-the one since dead, the other, dead to me, though still in the land of the living.

question: What was the greatest gathering of people you ever stood in?
answer: The largest concourse of people I ever beheld assembled in Hyde Park, on Sunday afternoon, some years back, to witness a great Chartist demonstration. I believe there were not fewer than 300,000 persons present.

question: Where do you expect to end your days?
answer: I have no objection to ending them in Scotland.
